newsitem.title: USA: Florida consumer confidence hits 7-year high.
newsitem.headline: Florida consumer confidence hits 7-year high.

text.p: Florida's consumer confidence index rose one point in February to 96, the highest level in seven years, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.
The confidence level was up seven points from a year ago, driven largely by strong faith in the national economy, said university economist Dave Denslow.
"This growing confidence pervades all groups of Floridians, young and old, low-income and high-income, dropouts and college graduates, but is stronger for women than for men," Denslow said.
Over the last year, the index has risen 11 points for women but only five points among men.

The share of respondents saying their personal financial condition had improved in the past year was down slightly. But the drop was more than offset by a larger share who expected the national economy to strengthen over the coming year and the next five years.
The positive outlook makes recession increasingly unlikely this year, despite high debt levels among consumers, Denslow said.

"Even though consumers still face record levels of household debt, gains in jobs and wages make many willing to take on more," said Chris McCarty, survey director at the university's Bureau of Economic and Business Research.
An interest rate increase could be a potential roadblock, dissuading many consumers from taking on more debt, he said.
Florida retailers, who have seen a rebound after a weak holiday season, should see benefits, the economists said.
"We expect consumers to continue their purchasing through March and most likely April as well," McCarty said.

The survey showed a boost in confidence across all regions, although employed respondents gave mixed reports about business condidtions for February. The share reporting that business was better than at the same time last year rose slightly to 50 percent, but the share who expect more employees to be hired in their workplace fell three points to 31 percent in February.
The monthly survey was based on telephone surveys among 921 randomly selected Florida adults and has an error margin of about three points.
The index uses 1966 as a base year, with numbers above 100 indicating consumers are more confident than they were then, and numbers below 100 indicating lesser confidence.
